problems.title: Most deep runs end in a soft lock: the run is not over, but no dig you can see is affordable
problems.evidence: `mineFuelCheck`/`mineCanGrow` compare the tank with `mineCheapestCost`, which is priced at the SHALLOWEST strand (2), while every dig at the working front costs 4-8. So a tank of 2-7 water at 84 m or deeper gives endless 'Not enough water - a dig here costs 8' toasts and the run never ends. Hit in runs 2, 3, 5, 8 and 11, and in 3 of 4 exploratory runs. Controlled probe (probe_softlock.cjs): 6 water at 93 m, idle 60 s, runOver=false (shots/softlock_probe_60s.png). The only exits are a worm draining the rest (runs 2 and 8), the rot deadline (run 3), or gear > End run (run 5, after 13.5 s of dead time). The intended recovery, digging from a surface strand, needs about 2000 px of panning at zoom 0.6, and nothing on screen suggests it.
problems.suggestion: End the run (after the grace period) when the tank cannot pay for a dig at the colony's working front: price it at the deepest tip or the camera-focus strand, not the shallowest. At minimum, show a large 'Spore now' button whenever water < costHere, so the ending is one tap.

problems.title: The game's only instruction is invisible on every phone, and a tap does nothing
problems.evidence: mineFrame (~line 37295) calls ui.setHint('Drag from the colony to dig'), but the CSS at ~lines 1011 and 693 sets `.hint { display: none; }` for max-width 760px. On a fresh run with isMobile and touch the hint's computed display is 'none' at 1.5, 4 and 8 s (probe_hint.cjs; run1/b_runstart.png shows no text). With true touch taps (probe_tap.cjs), tapping the colony and tapping open ground change nothing: no dig, no toast. Only a drag digs. A brand-new phone player sees a 10 px root under a hill and no words.
problems.suggestion: Give the mine hint its own element, or override the phone rule for the mine. Also make a plain tap on or near the colony dig downward (mineGrow already treats no direction as down), or at least toast 'drag to dig'.

problems.title: Run 1 cannot buy anything: the first store visit is seven greyed-out tiles
problems.evidence: First-run payouts on fresh saves were 9 P (run 1), 6, 12, 6 and 9 (exploratory saves). The cheapest item is 10 P (Water, Ore yield). 4 of 5 first runs could afford nothing (run1/i_store.png, every button disabled). CLAUDE.md Phase 4 says 'Run 1 ... banks one upgrade'. Runs 9 and 11 also bought nothing (13 P and 21 P against second rungs of 22-45 P).
problems.suggestion: Price the first rung of 2-3 tracks at 5-6 P, or give a first-descent bonus, so the first store visit always ends in a purchase. Keep the second rungs within about 1.5 runs of income.

problems.title: Only the first 42 m pays spendable money; depth pays unnamed materials with nothing to buy
problems.evidence: Every Phosphorus seam in all 11 runs was claimed at 10-46 m (strand depth). Below 42 m, seams pay anthracite, garnet or hematite and no P (mineOreRewards `isP`). `orePerPile` [3,5,8,12] ('deeper ore is worth more') is effectively dead for bands 1-3. The materials only buy heat rung 3 and above, enzyme rung 3 and above, or grow rung 4 and above, each behind 58+ P of earlier rungs. After run 11 the bank held 62 anthracite, 24 garnet and 6 hematite with nothing to spend them on. They appear as bare coloured dots with no name: the store header reads '✦29 ●53 ●21 ●6' (run10/i_store.png), the end screen '+8● +2●' (run4/h_end.png), and the HUD '●6' is clipped at the edge. Seams are drawn as the same orange leaf litter in every band, so a garnet seam looks like a phosphorus one. The game celebrates depth ('YOUR DEEPEST DESCENT YET', heat tolerance) while the money sits in the first band.
problems.suggestion: Let deep seams also pay P scaled by band (orePerPile already exists), or put a deep material on rung 1-2 of something desirable, so a first anthracite seam has an immediate use. Name the materials on the end screen, the store header and the HUD, and tint the seam art per material. The plan's own interlock ('materials want the compass; do not ship 6 alone') is showing.

problems.title: Upgrades are too small to feel, and progression is slower than the variance between seeds
problems.evidence: Water +5 on 84 (6%, 2.5 digs) for 10 P. After 10 runs and 8 purchases, start water went 84 -> 94. Depth by run: 82, 112, 96, 101, 89, 103, 112, 132, 132, 144. Runs 1-3 on identical upgrades already spread 82-112 m. Income was 8-24 P a run (132 P over 10 runs), about one small purchase per run, and none in runs 9 and 11. Every run felt the same: same hill, same ~100 m wall of 8-water digs.
problems.suggestion: Make early rungs visibly change a run (for example Water +15-20, Grow strength as the headline). Consider fewer, chunkier rungs, plus one per-run surprise (a modifier, a bonus seam, or a goal such as 'bring back 2 garnet').

problems.title: The Mucus flask is almost worthless at the level a player can buy
problems.evidence: excrete() gives one hit and `stickTurns` 1 (one 500 ms tick), and `killHits` is 3. Controlled probe (probe_counter.cjs): 2.0 water drained in the 10 s before the flask, 1.9 in the 10 s after, the worm still attached, toast 'Mucus burst - 1 stuck fast'. In runs 3 and 4 the worm was still attached after the flask (attached 1 -> 1). It is the first purchase a bitten player makes (15 P) and it saved 0.1 water. Worms also attach from off screen (run 2: attached at 21.3 s, first seen at 22.8 s) and are 16 px pale squiggles at the resting zoom (shots/look_worm.png, look_worm_zoom.png).
problems.suggestion: In the mine, have one flask detach or kill every worm within range (for example killHits 1, or a long stick that stops feeding). Draw attached worms larger or pulsing, and make the HUD worm chip point toward them.

problems.title: Mould ends about half the later runs early, avoiding it barely helps, and one enzyme dose often cannot cure
problems.evidence: Infections in 7 of 11 runs, at 29-42 s, including 5 of the 7 runs (6, 7, 9, 10, 11) after the player learned to route around cloud bodies: clouds hunt the colony within a 300-unit sight radius and also eat ore seams. Run 10 was infected at 29 s with 74 water in the tank and was over 20 s later. The enzyme cured a fresh 7-strand breach in the probe, but in the real run 11 the breach was already 46 strands at first detection; one centred cut took 40 and the clock ran on (run11/k_amp_armed.png, h_end.png shows 1 s left).
problems.suggestion: Sell two doses at rung 1, or make the cut radius follow the rotten filaments. Give the first infection of a save a longer clock. Make cloud sight rings readable enough, and routes wide enough, that avoidance is a real skill.

problems.title: Dev buttons are live on the plain URL and destroyed a run
problems.evidence: CONFIG.dev.enabled + inGameButtons: 'Dev: maps ▾' and 'Dev: edit rocks' sit top-right in every run (for example run1/b_runstart.png). 'Dev quick-start', 'Dev: unlock all' and 'Dev: +10,000 spores' float over the store, covering the MYCELIUM title and hovering over the tiles when scrolled (run4/j_store_bottom.png). In run 12 a drag near the top-right opened Dev: maps and loaded an amethyst campaign map inside the mine HUD. The run was lost (16 P, 9 anthracite): 0 m, cannot dig, no end screen (run12/x_stuck.png).
problems.suggestion: Gate the dev buttons behind a hash or query flag, not the release config, before anyone outside plays it.

problems.title: The HUD overflows the phone width, pushing the Settings gear (the only End run) off screen
problems.evidence: With the worm chip and the rot countdown both showing at 106 m, the resource pill is 423 px wide in a 390 px viewport. The dig price is clipped, the material row sits at x=439 and the gear at x=502, and elementFromPoint at the gear's centre returns null (probe_hud.cjs, shots/hud_full.png). The same crowding shows in run3/e_infected.png and run10/e_infected.png. Worms plus a deep soft lock is exactly when the player needs End run.
problems.suggestion: Wrap the pill onto two rows on narrow screens, or move depth and materials to a second row. Keep the gear pinned independently of the pill.

problems.title: 'Replay tutorial' in the mine silently restarts the run with no tutorial and no payout
problems.evidence: probe_menu.cjs: 13 m into a run with 3 P dug, gear > Replay tutorial left the player at 84 water and 1 m on a fresh map, with no tutorial and nothing banked (shots/menu_after_tutorial.png). It is the most natural tap for a confused newcomer.
problems.suggestion: Hide 'Replay tutorial' in the mine, or make it show the mine's instruction overlay without touching the run.

problems.title: Wrong or confusing copy at the edges
problems.evidence: End run from the menu gives cause 'abandon', and the end screen says 'The colony was eaten' (run5/h_end.png; eaten = died && cause !== 'dry'). After Save & exit, the title still reads 'DIG - start a new descent', but DIG resumes the old run. The load gate says 'CLICK' on a phone (shots/00a_loading.png). The 42 m band beat 'ANTHRACITE' does not say that digs now cost 4; only the chip's colour changes (explore1/f_heat_line.png).
problems.suggestion: Give the abandon its own end line ('You called the colony up'). Say 'continue your descent' when a resume exists. Use 'Tap' on touch devices. Add '- digs now cost 4' to the beat when a heat line coincides.

problems.title: End screen layout breaks when deep materials are present
problems.evidence: Run 1's end screen shows a small ✦. With any material present the Phosphorus sparkle renders about 100 px tall, and the unlabeled material dots drop to a second line (run4/h_end.png, run10/h_end.png, run11/h_end.png). The red all-caps call to action reads like an error.
problems.suggestion: Constrain the icon size and lay the earnings out as one labelled row ('+12 Phosphorus · +8 Anthracite · +2 Garnet').

problems.title: No collection feedback on the map
problems.evidence: Seams and pockets pay out with no floating number, pop or flash at the site; only the HUD digit changes (run1/d_first_ore.png: ✦3 with nothing marking which seam paid). Tapped water pockets look the same as untapped ones, so a player cannot tell which are spent.
problems.suggestion: Float '+3 ✦' or '+10 💧' at the seam or pocket, and dim or drain a pocket's art once tapped.

problems.title: A dig can grow from a different strand than the one pressed
problems.evidence: growDirected (~line 16290) falls through to 'any tip that can take a first step' when the pressed strand is walled in along the aim. So a dig aimed into rock can appear somewhere else and still charge, and it is priced at the pressed strand's depth rather than where it grew. In exploratory run 0, a simple always-dig-down bot spent 30 successful digs (60 water) stuck at 31-33 m, each one 'succeeding'.
problems.suggestion: In the mine, refuse ('Solid rock that way') when the pressed strand cannot step within the dodge fan, rather than growing from another tip.

problems.title: Nothing at the bottom: no goal once the depth record stops moving
problems.evidence: probe_bottom.cjs dug to 167 m of 168 with unlimited water: no reward, no message, no ending; digs just cost 16 (shots/bottom.png). The player's best went 112 -> 144 m over runs 2-10, so at this rate a player reaches the floor within roughly 15-20 runs, and then the one goal the game has is gone. Phase 3 (islands, journey east) is the plan's answer and is not built.
problems.suggestion: Until Phase 3 exists, make the floor a destination: a core event, a large one-time payout, or a reward for the first time you touch 168 m. Add a per-run objective so a run that doesn't beat the record still counts.

positives: The core gesture is good: a drag from the colony grows immediately, the growth looks organic, and the camera keeps the tip in the upper third with the route below visible (run1/g_midrun.png).

The descent is beautiful and reads as a journey: brown earth, then coal black, then garnet, then rust, each band with its own rock set, and a '42 m ANTHRACITE' beat at each band line (explore1/f_heat_line.png, run8/g_midrun2.png, shots/bottom.png).

Runs are short and restarting is fast: 45-80 s at a brisk pace, and end screen -> 'To the store' -> 'DESCEND' is two taps. The returning title shows 'deepest descent 144 m' and an UPGRADES link (run11/a_title.png).
The HUD numbers are honest whole numbers: water, the dig price (orange once heat applies), the worm drain rate ('1 -0.2/s') and the rot countdown are always stated.
Full payout on every ending, including the rot deadline, so no run feels wasted in currency.
No unwinnable seeds: 12 seeds flood-filled from the colony root all reach the 168 m floor, with 82-99% of open ground connected (probe_reach.cjs).
Run 1 lands close to the owner's target: a first descent reached 82 m in 51 s and ended cleanly without a soft lock.
The enzyme works cleanly on a fresh breach (7 rotten strands -> 0 with one cut, and the clock cleared) and the arm-then-tap flow is clear ('Tap where to cut.').
Store tiles are plain and each says exactly what it does, with DESCEND above the fold.
Performance is fine in headless Chromium: 60 fps at the start, about 50 fps with 700 strands and 16 worms (p95 33 ms).
0.loopVerdict:
There is a decent 45-60 second arcade descent here for the first two or three runs. It is pretty, the price is readable, there is a band beat every 42 m, and the drag feels good. But nothing yet pulls a player into run 11, let alone run 100.

(1) Most deep runs do not end. They soft-lock at 2-7 water against an 8-water dig, and the only escape (gear > End run) is often pushed off the phone screen by the HUD.
(2) A new phone player gets no instruction: the one hint is hidden by CSS, and a tap does nothing.
(3) The first store visit sells nothing (9 P against a 10 P minimum). Later visits sell 6% improvements: start water went 84 -> 94 over ten runs, and depth went 82 -> 144 m, less than the run-to-run spread between seeds.
(4) All spendable money is in the first 42 m, while the game celebrates depth. What depth pays out is unnamed coloured dots (62 anthracite banked by run 11) that the store will not take for several more rungs.
(5) The two counterplay items do little at the level you can afford. The flask saved 0.1 water. One enzyme dose failed on a real 46-strand breach. Meanwhile mould ended about half the later runs early (7 of 11 runs infected), even when the player routed around the clouds.
(6) Depth is the only goal, it caps at 168 m, and there is nothing at the floor.

As a returning player I was bored by about run 5 or 6: the purchases dry up, every run is the same hill, the same drag and the same ~100 m wall, and the last seconds are dead time.

What would make someone play run 11:
- A clean ending (auto-spore, or a big 'Spore now' button, when the front can't afford a dig) and a visible first instruction.
- A guaranteed first purchase, and early rungs you can feel.
- Deep seams paying Phosphorus by band (the unused orePerPile), with named materials that have an early use.
- A flask and enzyme that actually solve their threat at rung 1.

What would make someone play run 100: a destination and variety. That means the Phase 3 journey east plus the compass so the maze becomes decisions, a payoff at the floor, and per-run objectives or modifiers so a run that does not beat the depth record still counts.

Caveat: these runs were played by a sighted route-planning bot using real drag gestures at about 1.4 s per dig. A human is probably 1.5-2x slower, which makes worm drain and the 20 s rot clock proportionally harsher, not kinder.

1.summary:
The Deep Mine is a third CONFIG.game that runs on the old campaign engine. Everything that makes it a mine is in two places: __m_engine_mine (index.html 21309-22750: generation, economy, grow, heat, weapons, infection deadline, run end) and a set of mine branches in __m_main (32146-40557: configForLevel mine block 32461-32493, beginMineRun 32747, advanceSim streaming 37068-37074, mineFrame 37281, camera 37143-37239, presentMineEnd 33215). Everything else is borrowed: the substrate, growDirected, stepNematodes and infectNetwork, buildLevel/stampFood, the store and the HUD. setGame('mine') (3823) forces real time and turns off cards.enabled, and that one switch removes the card layer.

The world is a grid allocated once at 504x168 cells. Its content streams in per chunk (mineEnsureChunks, called every frame, runs mineGenerateChunk: carve first, then place rock sprites). Collision is drawn from sprite alpha into a fine mask during render (solidifyRock, then solidifyMineRock adds new sprites incrementally).

The plain URL shows a mine-only title screen: a "Dig" button (#tsNewMine), "deepest descent N m" or "water is your fuel", Upgrades (only when minerals > 0) and Credits. Dig goes straight into a run; the store appears only after a descent ends.

Measured in this container (headless, software raster, 390x844):
- Boot to Click: 1.1 s, 159 requests. Fine mask ready 1.4 s after the click.
- renderFrame: 8.5 ms fresh, 12 ms at 120 strands, 24 ms at 5000 strands.
- tickWorld: about 4-6 ms, flat, set by five full passes over all 85k cells per tick.
- Generating 3 chunks at once made one 95 ms long task.
- mine-check baseline: 186 passed, 4 failed in 4m58s. Three are the documented box-in ceilings ("28 m on 98 digs"). The fourth: the band-beat dive only reached 78 m.

Blocking problems I confirmed while mapping:
1. Release pipeline. A copy of make-web-zip's prune logic (run against the repo, nothing written) drops assets/magnetite-c24 and assets/garnet-c24, so a zip would ship bands 0 and 2 without rock art or collision. itchzip-check still clicks #tsNewCamp/#tsNew, which the mine-only title does not render. With dev.enabled=false, which is what a zip ships, the campaign's black "Level" card appears before every descent and pauses the game until clicked.
2. Collision before the mask. On a throttled link (about 1.6 Mbps), the map is playable 4.1 s after Dig but the rock mask lands at 39.8 s. Three digs in that window left 11 of 50 strands inside rock.
3. Node cap. growth.maxNodes 6000 is shared with the card game. At the cap every dig fails with "Solid rock that way" while water remains, so the run cannot end on fuel.
4. Taps are dead in the mine. endPointer returns at 36700, so a plain tap never digs, never commits an armed enzyme cut (only a drag does), and double-tap never reframes. CLAUDE.md says tap = dig down; that only works through the hooks.
5. Wrong end-screen copy and a lost run. The settings "End run" ends the descent as cause 'abandon' and the end screen says "The colony was eaten". "Save & exit" drops to the title with the run still alive and the ore not banked; the mine has no resume. "Replay tutorial" does nothing.
6. End-screen icon. The Phosphorus icon on the end screen renders full-width because .ss-win-earned has no .ss-ri size rule.

For Phase 3, the hooks are all there: the home-column logic (buildLevel 19412, mineGenerateChunk `home` 21620/21755/21817/22007), mineLevelDef, the startRun seed, mineEndRun causes, presentMineEnd, and loadProgress defaults. The hard parts are a guaranteed lateral route that does not turn into a visible corridor, and compass data for chunks that have not been generated yet.

Probes, screenshots and the mine-check log are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-myceliumRT/a2f5e2e3-decc-5856-aa55-dec16f4b83e6/scratchpad/architect/:
- probe.cjs, probe2.cjs, probe3.cjs, probe4.cjs, prune-sim.mjs
- A-title.png, A-firstframe.png, C-release-first-frame.png, D-endrun.png, D-store.png, E-slownet.png
- mine-check.log

1.runLifecycle:
BOOT. __m_main runs at load. It calls showLoading (40485) and preloads the eager manifest plus _bootImgs (40486: all 71 card faces, 19 species portraits, gnome layers, tutorial portraits; 159 requests, 1.1 s locally) through Promise.all at 40548, with a 12 s safety net. requestAnimationFrame(frame) starts at 40554, and frame idles while state is null. _bootReady (40526) logs 'boot', and the loader's click runs initMusic, initSfx and enterGame (40423). enterGame parses the hash: '#mine[,seed]' calls beginMineRun, then, if a seed was given, sets mineSeed and calls startRun again (40446-40450); anything else calls showMainMenu (33691).

MENU (plain URL). showTitleScreen (29678) renders mineMenu (29737) because OFFER_CAMPAIGN and OFFER_SURVIVAL are both false: a 'Dig' button (#tsNewMine), then 'deepest descent N m' (p.mineBest) or 'water is your fuel', an 'Upgrades' header button (only if p.minerals > 0, 29889; it calls setGame('mine') and showPicker), and Credits. There is no mine resume or 'Old'. CONFIG.game is still 'survival' on the title. Dig calls onNew(name,'realtime','mine') (30571 -> 33709): setMode, setGame('mine') (3823: realtime on, cards.enabled off), no resetProgress for the mine (33719), then beginMineRun (33725).

RUN START. beginMineRun (32747) sets game, clears the playtest/species/sandbox globals, sets mineSeed = Date.now()&0x7fffffff (32751), mineBeatBand = -1, runs stockRun (retries, irrelevant to the mine), logs run_start {level 1, cause 'new'}, and calls startRun (32735). startRun raises the handoff curtain and calls start(mineSeed) (32742). start (32635) does four things:
1. configForLevel(currentLevel) (32432) deep-clones CONFIG and, in the mine block (32461-32493), writes sightRadius 300 onto both threats, nematodes.maxPopulation 16, the trych overrides, then store bonuses from storeBonuses() (14410): startWater += water track, growSteps, reservoirWater += pocketWater, oreBonus, items {excrete, amputate}, heatBonus.
2. levelDefFor (32607) returns mineLevelDef(CONFIG, mineSeed) (21545): world box 504x168 cells, layout.mine, zero threat ceilings with respawn:false, no objects, assetsFromAll for the 4 bands.
3. loadLevelAssets for each band folder (32650), not awaited.
4. begin(createLevelState(cfg, seed, def)). createLevelState (19685) runs configForLevelDef (19280: mine box, coreDepthFrac 1), then buildLevel (19392: sub.mine, mineHomeCol = cols>>1, hill soil, no goal columns), Network.seed at the home column (the Network constructor sets water = mine.startWater, 15889), mineOre/mineItems/mineMats (19710), then assembleState.
begin (35184) builds the renderers (SubstrateRenderer goes live), reassigns window.__game (35217, mine hooks at 35401), builds or points the UI at the mine HUD, parks the camera on the root at mineZoom() (35799), and arms pendingLevelIntro (35869). revealMap (32266) skips that card only when dev.enabled is true, so a release build shows 'Level ...' here. start() then calls mineArmCamera and mineEnsureChunks(state) (32657-32660), which generates the home chunk and its neighbours (about 2k sprites) before the first frame. solidifyRock (39091) runs inside renderFrame once every sprite has decoded, publishing _fineSolid and keeping _coarseCover and _solidFrom for the mine.

CHUNKS. mineEnsureChunks (22325) runs from advanceSim every frame (37068-37074) along with mineNoteDig and solidifyMineRock. It wants the home chunk, every chunk within preloadCols (26) of the colony's x extent, and every chunk inside the camera span. For each missing chunk it calls mineGenerateChunk(state, ci) (21610), seeded by mineChunkRng(seed, ci) (21587), in this order: galleries at rows 3+18k in segments with seam seals (21655-21732); broken shafts, the home one starting at the home column (21733-21779); links (21780-21813); the home head (21814-21825); per-band ore spurs, pocket spurs and dead ends (21827-21920); plugs (21922-21993); the flood-and-repair descent guarantee, home chunk only (21995-22064); the stranded sweep, which counts and does not delete (22066-22111). Then it stamps ore with stampFood (tagged pile.mineMat by band) and pockets with stampReservoir (22113-22131), pushes rock sprites onto sub.levelSprites (OVERLAP 0.94, sized to slabs) plus a guaranteed sprite per plug (22133-22269), and places worms and clouds from threatBands (22276-22311). The chunk record goes to state.mineChunks[ci], and the dirty column range is recorded for solidifyMineRock (39234), which stamps the new sprites incrementally and reconciles cell.rock and water over that range.

TICK. advanceSim (37047) accumulates wall time and calls tickWorld(state) every 500 ms (37102-37106, up to 3 catch-up ticks, paused while any menu, intro or tutorial is up: simPaused 36981). tickWorld (22780) runs:
- spreadTrichoderma (18125): clouds creep and eat.
- stepAnts (18785): no-op.
- stepNematodes (17560): the mine branch attaches worms, drains 0.2 W/s each through mineDrainDebt, breeds at 5%/s capped at 16, and sets state.mineAttached.
- resolveTraps (card residue).
- Per network: colonizeReachablePiles while a grow is in flight (22828); resolveIncome (the mine fast path over foodPiles, 23030); agePass; infectNetwork (18330, the rot creeping with the mine's overrides); starvation; the vitality and death checks (cause 'infected' or 'devoured' builds its own runResult without depth).
- Ward aging over every cell (22881). State.cards is absent, so no card engines run.
After the tick: renderer dirty flags, checkWater (a no-op in the mine), and presentRunOver if the run is over.
EVERY FRAME, mineFrame (37281) runs while unpaused:
- A one-time hint 'Drag from the colony to dig', shown until p.mineBest > 0.
- mineFollowCamera (37198).
- mineOreRewards (22376): a claimed, empty pile under clean cover pays its material, and Phosphorus also credits net.phosphorus and state.mineOre.
- mineWaterPickups (22418): +reservoirWater once per pocket.
- mineDepthReached into state.mineDepth.
- mineBeat (37244, 'NN m / Band' through showMineBeat).
- mineFuelCheck (22703: cannot afford the CHEAPEST dig (mineCheapestCost) for 1600 ms) leads to mineEndRun(state,'dry'). Otherwise mineInfectionCheck (22582: a 20 s wall-clock deadline that runs while anything is infected) leads to mineEndRun(state,'infected').

GROW GESTURE. pointerdown (36624) calls beginAim (36402). armedDragTarget (36385) always returns {kind:'mine'}. A press within aimNearPx of a strand starts an aim snapped to it; a press farther away pans (pointermove 36645 -> panByScreen + mineReleaseCamera). pointermove updates the aim with updateAim (36433). Release (endPointer 36675) calls fireAim(a) (36474), but only if the pointer dragged at least 12 px and did not go out and back; a plain tap returns at 36691 or 36700 and does nothing. fireAim runs mineArmedTap (36460, the armed enzyme cut) first, else mineGrow(state, {srcX, srcY, x, y}) (22456). mineGrow refuses when the pressed strand is infected, prices the dig at the source strand's depth with mineGrowCost (22620: base 2, doubling past heat lines at 42 m plus heatBonus and every 42 m after, capped at x8), refuses when water is short, calls net.growDirected(sub, rng, dx, dy, growSteps*3, false, tip) (16249), deducts water, and stamps state._mineFocus. mineNoteDig then re-arms the camera. The aim arrow is drawAimLine (40341) at mineGrowReach. The kit buttons (26425-26427) go to handlers.onMineItem (35957): the flask calls mineUseExcrete (22549); the enzyme arms state._mineArmed, and the next DRAG release calls mineUseAmputate (22563, cutRadius 220).

CAMERA. mineZoom (37143) is 0.6 x viewH/844. Wheel, pinch and F go through mineClampZoom (37161) to zoomRange [0.4, 2.2] x rest, and mineReleaseCamera. mineFollowCamera (37198) does nothing while the camera is released; otherwise it eases zoom back to rest and x/y to the _mineFocus node (falling back to the deepest clean tip), with a downward look-ahead scaled by the dig's dy. The play surface is boxed to the 390:844 aspect (playSurfaceRect 36893, resize 36901).

RUN END. mineEndRun (22714) computes depth and ore, turns every strand infected if the cause was 'infected', sets fruited, alive=false, runOver, and runResult {mine, depth, ore, mats copy, died:false, cause 'dry'|'infected'}. Other endings reach presentRunOver too: tickWorld deaths (cause 'devoured' or 'infected', died:true) and the settings 'End run' button (forceFruitAbandon 33063, cause 'abandon', died:true). presentRunOver (33260) waits for the last reveal (at most 2.8 s), then calls clearResume and presentMineEnd(r) (33215). presentMineEnd takes depth and ore from r or else from state, banks once (_minePaid): addSpores(ore) writes p.minerals, addMats writes p.mats. It logs run_end {level: depth, cause, n: ore}, records mineRecordDepth (33251, p.mineBest), and calls showMineEnd (29281). The end screen grows 'SPORED', prints the depth, one cause line (branched on the cause, but 'abandon' falls into the 'eaten' copy), and +P and +mats (the P icon is unsized), with a 'To the store' button. That button calls runEndThen (32930: endRunSpores, recordRunFinished), then setGame('mine') and showPicker().

STORE. showPicker (32774) calls showSpeciesSelect({mine:true}) (28961): the header 'The Deep Mine', a P wallet plus held mats, a Descend button with the note '84 water to start · grow 2 · 2 water a dig', and a shelf of STORE_UPGRADES filtered by upgradeInGame (14249: MINE_UPGRADE_IDS = water, growSteps, heatTolerance, excreteCharges, amputateCharges, oreYield, pocketWater). Each tile's price comes from upgradeCosts (MINE_COSTS re-prices water); costParts (14313) reads a number as P and {m,n} as n of material m. buyUpgrade (14323) checks costBalance, then writes p.mineUpgrades[id] and debits p.minerals or p.mats, returning {ok, paid|need}. The 'upgrade' event is logged in renderUpgrades (29204). Purchases reach the next run only through configForLevel.

NEXT RUN. Descend (29220) calls onPick(null,1), then beginMineRun with a fresh Date.now seed. Every run is a new random shaft; only a URL seed pins one.

Everything lives in localStorage 'mycelium.progress.v2' (13683), shared with the retired games: minerals, mineUpgrades, mats, mineBest, runsDone, and the campaign fields (spores, upgrades, deck, clears, purchased...). loadProgress (13685) fills defaults and migrateProgress (13719) runs flag-guarded migrations. risks: RELEASE IS BROKEN FOR THE MINE, and nothing in the repo's gates can see it: (a) the prune drops two of the four band folders; (b) itchzip-check drives title rows that no longer exist; (c) the dev-off build shows a campaign 'Level' card before every run. All the checks run with dev.enabled true against the full asset tree. Fix all three before any upload.

COLLISION IS NOT READY WHEN THE MAP IS: solidAtWorld falls back to cell.rock, which is empty on a mine map until solidifyRock has every sprite decoded, and revealMap does not wait for _rockSolidified. Measured on a ~1.6 Mbps throttled link: map visible and diggable 4.1 s after Dig, mask at 39.8 s; three digs left 11 of 50 strands inside rock (E-slownet.png). Gate the reveal, or mineGrow, on sub._rockSolidified, and/or preload the four band folders during the boot loader instead of the card faces.

LONG-RUN SCALING: growth.maxNodes 6000 soft-locks a run that still has water (every dig refused). Render cost grows with strands (8.5 ms fresh -> 24 ms at 5000 in software raster). There are about 7 O(nodes) passes per frame plus waterSourcesNear at O(25*nodes) per frame. Late runs of 3-5 minutes with upgraded grow (up to 7 steps = 21 segments a dig) will reach thousands of nodes.

STREAMING HITCHES: mineGenerateChunk is synchronous on the main thread, about 30 ms per chunk (95 ms long task for 3 chunks when the camera jumped), and it runs on exactly the frames the player is watching. Compass work that needs plans for ungenerated chunks makes this worse; a pure plan/stamp split (possibly in a Worker) is the lever, but it must preserve rng call order.

GENERATOR INVARIANTS ARE LOAD-BEARING and easy to break silently. Galleries sit at world-fixed rows 3+18k and are pinned at the seams. Sprites must fit inside their own chunk. The rock centre is clamped to its band. Plugs run after spurs, and the repair runs after plugs. Chunk generation must be order-independent. Rng call order defines every seed, so any reorder changes every pinned-seed assertion and every measured fuel curve. Density changes have moved startWater three times (20->30->44->84).

BOX-IN WITH NO COUNTERPLAY: at 44% solid a colony can dig itself into a pocket it cannot leave. mine-check has three standing failures for this ('28 m on 98 digs'); baseline today is 186 passed / 4 failed in 4m58s (the fourth is the band-beat dive stopping at 78 m). The premise 'rock is a wall' forbids rock-eating, while the generator's comments keep sealed seams as bait for exactly that; the owner must resolve it.

40k-LINE SINGLE FILE WITH DECLARATION-ORDER DEPENDENCIES: modules can only import from earlier IIFEs, so stepNematodes reads sub.mine and config.mine instead of the mine module, and a const in one IIFE is invisible in another (BUILD_ID once crashed boot). window.__game is rebuilt in every begin(), and the HUD calls it (27194). About 25% of the file (cards data, levels data, tutorial, loadout, highscores, campaign screens) is residue, but threaded through it are hard dependencies (infectNetwork, amputateAt, waterSourcesNear, excrete, buildLevel). Edits need grep-before-touch and a full `node tests/run.mjs --mine` (about 5-6 min).

CONTAINER ROLLBACKS (CLAUDE.md 4871-4981): the working tree, local refs and scratchpad are periodically restored to hours- or days-old snapshots, sometimes mid-edit or disguised as uncommitted work. Commit and push each piece as it stands up. Before resetting, `git fetch origin <branch>` first; `git rev-parse HEAD origin/<branch> && ls tests/ | wc -l` is the tell; never commit a dirty tree you did not write.

TEST BRITTLENESS: mine-check is 2460 lines of long-lived shared pages whose probes navigate a maze (__digTo/__aimDown). Once-per-run events (the band beat, pockets) can only be measured from a fresh page. Probes that measure water must zero the worm drain and the respawns. run.mjs treats '0 passed 0 failed' as green (aim can silently assert nothing in a sweep). Several assertions pin world shape (root at cols>>1, lateral bounds, chunk counts) and will break on purpose with Phase 3; change them deliberately and record why, as CLAUDE.md does. Career R8 reached 107 m and the end screen said 99 m (career-cheap-r8-end.png). The threat probe reached 63 m and the screen said 50 m (threat-rot-end.png). The deepest-descent record (p.mineBest) is saved from the same number.
problems.suggestion: Track the maximum clean depth reached during the run (a running max in mineFrame) and pay and record that. Rot should not erase progress already made.

problems.title: 'Save & exit to menu' in the mine deletes the run and its haul
problems.evidence: menu.cjs: 45 m in, holding 9 P + 2 anthracite, pressed Save & exit. The title offered only 'Dig' (the mine has no 'Old'), and the wallet stayed at 0. Dig started a fresh descent at 84 water. Everything dug was lost, and nothing was banked. Screens: menu-set-saveexit.png, menu-saveexit-dig.png.
problems.suggestion: In the mine, either bank the haul and end the run (rename the item 'Fruit and exit') or hide the item. A 'Save' that deletes is the worst kind of button.

problems.title: The HUD overflows a 390 px phone and pushes the settings gear off screen
problems.evidence: hud.cjs, with worm, infection and material chips all showing: #gearbtn at x=530-562, #hud-digcost at 348-410 and .matchip at 431-461, on a 390 px viewport. The gear is the only way to reach 'End run', and it disappears exactly when worms or rot are in play. Even with no extra chips the cost chip wraps to '8 / a dig'. Screens: hud-full.png, threat-worms-attached.png, run1-4242-end.png (HUD cut at the right edge).
problems.suggestion: Wrap the pill onto a second row or collapse chips to icon + number. Keep the gear outside the pill's flow (position: fixed). Add a mine-check assertion that every HUD rect sits inside the viewport with all chips on.

problems.title: A new player's natural gesture burns the tank for nothing
problems.evidence: naive.cjs, 8 runs, always digging from the deepest tip (straight down, or toward the most open ray): median 28 m, range 14-75. It stalled by dig 12-20 with 44-60 water left, then spent the rest on digs that 'succeed' because the dodge fan finds sideways ground, gaining 0 m each. 8 of 8 runs banked 0-6 P, so the first store visit has nothing affordable (naive-aim-4242.png shows '+0'). This is what the tests' own greedy probes see (mine-probe copy: 1 -> 37 m over 40 digs on seed 909). The sensible router made 56-107 m on the same budget, so there is skill in the maze, but nothing teaches the player to back up and pick another strand.
problems.suggestion: Warn or refuse when a dig gains no new ground ('dead end - try another strand'), or refund part of a dig that made fewer than N new cells. Highlight the three best frontier strands for the first few runs. Guarantee run 1 at least 10 P, for example with a seam near the start column.

problems.title: The content runs out: the floor is reachable in under 80 s, and the store is a dead end
problems.evidence: The shaft is 168 m. Maxed runs reached 167 m in 48 s and 79 s, with 242 water unspent and a dig costing 2 at 149 m: heat tolerance of +150 m moves the first line to 192 m, deleting heat from a 168 m shaft. A greedy-buy model at 5-8 P seams per run exhausts the store in 56-89 runs (about 1-1.5 h at 1 min per run); from run 36-57 onward only the water track is left, at 225-500 P a rung for +5 water, which cannot matter to a player finishing runs with 200+ water. With the store exhausted: 6772 P and about 190 of each material, all unspendable (store-exhausted.png). Runs never lengthen either: 38-61 s from run 1 to run 14, against the plan's 3-5 minutes.
problems.suggestion: Ship Phase 3 (legs and islands) as the endless axis, with threat and density escalation per leg. Cap heat tolerance below the shaft depth, or deepen the shaft per leg. Cut the water track to about 5 rungs. Add a long-term sink or prestige for leftover currency, plus daily seeds and a depth-and-time board so run 100 has a reason.

problems.title: Dev buttons are live on the shipped branch; one credits 10,000 Phosphorus
problems.evidence: CONFIG.dev.enabled and dev.inGameButtons are both true. 'Dev: maps' and 'Dev: edit rocks' sit on the play screen in every screenshot. The store shows 'Dev quick-start', 'Dev: unlock all' and 'Dev: +10,000 spores' over the wordmark (store-fresh.png). The last one calls addSpores(DEV_SPORES), which in the mine writes the minerals wallet: one tap buys every P rung. The CONFIG comment says the Pages build serves this branch as-is.
problems.suggestion: Turn dev.enabled off for any public build. Relabel the button 'P' in the mine, or hide it there.

problems.title: 'End run' in the mine says 'The colony was eaten'
problems.evidence: forceFruitAbandon writes cause 'abandon' with died: true, so showMineEnd's `eaten` branch fires: '45m The colony was eaten. What it had spored is yours.' after a voluntary end with 56 water in the tank (menu-set-forcefruit.png). The payout itself is correct (9 P + 2 anthracite banked).
problems.suggestion: Give 'abandon' its own line, e.g. 'You ended the descent.' Or route the mine's End run through mineEndRun(state, 'abandon').

problems.title: End-screen glyphs: the Phosphorus star balloons and the materials are unlabelled
problems.evidence: RI.phos (class ss-ri) has no size rule inside .ss-win-earned, so the star renders about 55 px at +9 and about 170 px at +108 (tier-max-4242-end.png, career-cheap-r8-end.png). Deep materials show as '+32 dot', a tiny tinted dot with no name. The 'SPORED' wordmark is clipped at both edges at 390 px.
problems.suggestion: Size .ss-win-earned .ss-ri the way .spore-ic is sized (0.95em). Add the material name, or a 3-letter tag, next to each dot.

problems.title: Worms are barely visible at the resting zoom
problems.evidence: A worm is a roughly 10 px white squiggle on a 390x844 phone at zoom 0.6, and its olive sight wash barely shifts the soil (worm-crop.png, worm-frame.png). In mid-run frames an attached worm cannot be found by eye; only the '1 -0.2/s' chip says it is there (run1-1234-s02.png).
problems.suggestion: Draw worms at 2-3x in the mine (or add a pulsing ring when locked on), and mark the strand each attached worm is feeding on.

problems.title: Worm breeding switches off once the colony has explored four chunks
problems.evidence: maxPopulation 16 is checked against the global nematode count, but seeding is 4 worms per chunk (1+1+2). 3 chunks gives 12 worms, so breeding can happen. 4+ chunks gives 16+ (24 observed on run 1), so no worm ever breeds again. Isolated, the breeding is brutal: 3 -> 8 worms in 20 s, draining 27 water (one base tank in about 60 s). Exploring sideways silently turns breeding off.
problems.suggestion: Cap breeding per chunk, or cap it by attached worms rather than the world population. Then tune breedPerSec against the real number.

problems.title: Store copy doesn't match play
problems.evidence: The store note always says '2 water a dig' (ssMineNote), whatever the heat. The enzyme tile promises 'a small radius', but cutRadius is 220 units (6 cells) and one cut removed 118 strands. The flask tile says nothing about needing 3 hits.
problems.suggestion: Quote the heat ladder on the note ('2 / 4 / 8 / 16 past 42 / 84 / 126 m'). Describe the enzyme's cut as wide, and state the flask's 3-hit rule.

problems.title: First-run variance decides whether the store opens
problems.evidence: Sensible first runs: 56-107 m (1.9x spread) and 9-18 P (2x). Seed 11 banked 9 P, one short of the cheapest rung. The spread is driven by which pockets are found and whether worms attach (drained 0-7.6 water) or rot touches.
problems.suggestion: Guarantee the first descent at least one full rung, for example with a floor on run-1 P or a 5-P first rung.

positives: Run 1 meets its time target: 38-65 s and 33-43 digs on 8 seeds with a route-planning player.
Routing is a real skill: a player who plans a route reaches 56-107 m on run 1, against 14-75 m for one who drags from the bottom on the same 84 water.

No sealed pockets in practice. 0 of 39 route-planning runs found themselves boxed (the flood always found reachable ground), and the copied mine-probe measured 99.2-99.3% connectivity with 48 of 48 and 40 of 40 ore seams reachable. The '28 m on 98 digs' ceiling is the greedy deepest-tip probe, not the map.
The HUD makes the numbers readable: whole-number water, a live price chip that turns orange with heat, a worm chip that shows the drain rate, and an infection countdown in seconds.
Ore seams (orange) and water pockets (blue) are easy to spot on screen, and keeping them off the direct route makes detours a real decision.
Depth progression is felt early: the career's deepest run went from 60 m to 140 m in 12 runs, and each band change (brown, black, red, rust) is a visible milestone.
Full payout on every ending means no run feels stolen (every ending tested banked its ore, except Save & exit).

Stable: 0 page errors and 0 console errors across about 50 boots and 60+ descents. renderFrame measured 10-16 ms median, p90 up to 25 ms, at 800-1600 strands in headless software raster (copied mine-probe: 15.0 / 17.6 ms).
3.loopVerdict:
The 45-second dive works as a core: a counted tank, a doubling price, a maze to route through, and off-route rewards give each run 30-40 real decisions, and a player who plans beats one who doesn't by about 2x in depth. The loop around it is broken in ways that will show within the first 10-15 minutes.

**1. Runs can refuse to end.** In 36% of runs the player ends up holding 2-7 water in front of a '4 or 8 a dig' chip, and the run stays live. Nothing on screen explains why, and only a stray worm or a trip to the gear menu (which the HUD can push off screen) ends it. That is the first thing to fix.

**2. The currency comes from the wrong place.** Only the top 42 m pays Phosphorus, so P per run was flat at about 17 across 14 runs and 4 of 14 store visits bought nothing. Anthracite and garnet piled up at 160 and 56 against demands of 18 and 31. Staying shallow and going sideways earns about 2x more P than descending.

**3. The purchases are unbalanced.**
- Heat tolerance and Ore yield are the strong buys: 58 P buys about +35 m, and Ore yield doubles income while also quietly quadrupling deep materials.
- The water track is the weak buy: 1849 P, 57% of the shelf.
- Flask and enzyme rungs 1-2 are traps: one flask is a 0.5 s stun, and 1-2 doses cannot clear a breach.
- The infection costs almost nothing, because the tank can be dumped inside its 20 s window.
- Heat can be bypassed for 8x cheaper digs by pressing a strand that touches rock.

**4. There is no long game.** Fully upgraded runs hit the 168 m floor in 48-79 s with 240 water unspent. The store exhausts in about 56-89 runs, the last 20-30 of them buying water that cannot matter. After that there are thousands of unspendable P and nothing to chase except a depth record already at the cap.

**What would bring players back for run 11:**
- Fix the dry-for-deep softlock and the heat bypass.
- Make depth pay P, scaled by band, and give the deep materials real sinks.
- Make one flask or one dose decisive.
- Make the infection cost part of the haul.
- Cut the water track.

**What would bring them back for run 100:** an endless axis. Phase 3's legs east are the natural one: each leg a fresh shaft with rising density and threats and a deeper floor, the heat cap tied to the leg, plus daily seeds and a depth-and-time board. As built, a dedicated player sees everything in about an hour.

premises: The Deep Mine (CONFIG.game === 'mine') is the only game. Campaign and survival are retired from the title screen and from the checks but are NOT deleted. infectNetwork and its ring/depth/rot tuning are a dependency of the mine, so threat changes go BESIDE the existing machinery, never over it.

Rock is a WALL, not a material. Mycelium does not eat rock, so this is a maze-runner, not a digger. Every 'why not dig through it' idea is answered by that. The one owner-sanctioned exception is a later bought consumable, in the owner's words: 'it's totally fine if some areas are not reachable - we will have consumables later that allow people to grow through rocks when needed.'
There are NO RETURN TRIPS. The colony IS the map, spread across it. A run ends where it ends and the player advances rather than coming back. This is the genre position, not a gap.
Run 1 is under a minute (the plan says ~45 s) and banks ONE upgrade. Late runs are 3-5 minutes, tuned at the end. How long a late run is comes out of the costs pass; it is not an input to it.

No cards, no drafting, no deck. Real time. Portrait phone. One grow, always armed: drag from the colony to dig, and a tap with no direction digs down. Brief: start with grow 2 at 2 water, keep digging while there is water, hill in the middle, go deeper, rock types by depth. Running dry means the colony fruits and spores and the player goes to the upgrade store.

The owner's own reasons for the pivot: the cards 'made it too complex', there was 'too much card drafting', and dying 'felt like you lost too much'. They also want shorter initial loops. More onboarding polish is NOT the fix: it was tested and did nothing ('I've checked the data and the changes did nothing').
Count water and everything else only in whole numbers. Fractional rates such as the worm drain build up as a debt, and only whole units leave the tank.

Worms drain water instead of eating: 1 water per 5 s per attached worm, a 5%/s breed chance while feeding, population cap 16. Attachment is drawn on the strand and counted in the HUD along with its rate.

Threat sight rings are on by default: a plain flat fill, green 120,155,45 at alpha 0.15, with no outline, rim or gradient. Four treatments have been tried; do not add a fifth. sightRgb and sightAlpha move together. Creature sight radius is 300, so nothing senses the colony from off-screen.
Band 1 (the first 42 m) is threat-free on purpose. Worms appear from band 2, mould from band 3, no ants, and NOTHING RESPAWNS.

Trichoderma: ONE infection timer per colony (20 s) from first contact, derived from 'is anything infected'. It stops only when EVERY infected strand is gone; cutting one of two contact points keeps the clock running. Infected strands cannot be grown from. When the timer ends, the whole colony turns green, fruits, and the run pays out IN FULL.
Consumables are BOUGHT, and nothing is given. Mucus flasks and Cutting enzyme are sold as how many you carry, restocked every descent, not as charges that deplete across runs. A miss costs nothing.

Interlock: Amputate is bought AND forced fruiting pays out in full. Meeting mould with an empty bag ends the run early without taking anything away. Changing either one alone makes early mould brutal.

Heat is PRICED, NOT ENFORCED. Every dig past a depth line costs more water on a doubling staircase (lines at 42 m and every 42 m after, so 2, 4, 8, 16, capped by maxMult 8). Nothing burns off, and a dig the game allows always succeeds. Heat tolerance slides the ladder down. The price is set where the dig starts, affordability asks the cheapest ground, and the HUD always quotes the price.
Every depth band has its own soil colour: brown, then black, then red. The colour changes on the rock bands, not on the price lines.

Materials: one per band (Phosphorus, Anthracite, Garnet, Hematite), and the band decides the material. Phosphorus is the general currency. Deep rungs are priced in deep materials ('looking for the right materials for upgrades').
Interlock: materials want the compass. Without one, 'find garnet' is a random walk. Do not ship 06 alone.
Nothing worth having is on the way down. Ore and water pockets sit at the far ends of lateral galleries and spurs, off the descent route. A water pocket is a one-off +10 burst, not an annuity.
The maze is asymmetric: long east-west corridors and scarce north-south links, with plugs on the ways down. Heavier rock is fine, and some unreachable areas are fine.

A FRESH WORLD PER LEG, seeded by journey and leg index, with the hill at the WEST and the island at the EAST. The 504-column streamed map stays as it is, and eastward progress is a small integer rather than an ever-wider world.

Compasses are BOUGHT PER RESOURCE. Nothing is given, including the island compass, because the player already knows to go east; what is sold is precision. The rungs are direction, then direction and distance, then pointing at the BIGGEST deposit rather than the nearest. A compass MUST POINT THROUGH ROCK: a bearing, never a route.
Look anywhere, and a dig brings you back. Resting zoom is 0.6 and zoomRange [0.4, 2.2] is bounded by streaming. A pan releases the camera and a successful dig re-arms it.
The mine has New and no Old (no resume). The store is the persistence, and 'New' must never wipe the save. The mine's store is its own wallet (minerals) and ledger (mineUpgrades).
planRemaining: PROGRESS line (CLAUDE.md): `PHASES 1 AND 2 COMPLETE. Phase 3: (07) green islands and the journey east — next.`

7. **GREEN ISLANDS AND THE PROMISED LAND.** Islands scattered eastward; reach one, resurface and spore, and the next run starts from there. Surface resources barely fund the next leg, so the first runs must go DOWN to afford going RIGHT. **A FRESH WORLD PER LEG**, seeded by journey and leg index, hill at the WEST and island at the EAST — the 504-column streamed map stays as it is and eastward progress is a small integer rather than an ever-wider world.

07 (docs/mine-plan.html): Islands scattered eastward. Reach one, resurface and spore, and the next run starts from there. Surface resources barely fund the next leg, so the first runs have to go down to afford going right. Why it matters: It gives the world a second axis — depth is currently the only one — and it turns "no return trip" from a missing feature into the structure of the game. Shape: A fresh world per leg, seeded by journey and leg index, hill at the west and island at the east. Keeps the 504-column map that already works and makes "how far east am I" a small integer rather than a coordinate.

8. **COMPASSES, BOUGHT PER RESOURCE.** A needle for the next island and separately purchased tech per material. **Nothing is given, including the island compass** — a player without one still knows to go east, because that is the goal, so what is sold is *precision*. Rungs: direction → direction and distance → points at the BIGGEST deposit rather than the nearest. **IT MUST POINT THROUGH ROCK.** A bearing keeps the maze ("I know it is that way, now find the corridor"); a route would make the maze stop mattering.

08 (docs/mine-plan.html): A needle for the next island, and separately purchased tech for each material you want to track. Both are bought — nothing here is given. Selling information rather than power is the most distinctive progression idea in the game. A player with no compass is not lost, because east is the standing instruction: the promised land is that way and always was. What the compass sells is precision — exact bearing and distance — which is a much easier thing to price than the difference between having a direction and having none. Rungs fall out of one feature: direction → direction and distance → points at the biggest deposit rather than the nearest. It must point through rock. ... Why last: It's what makes 06 and 07 legible, so it wants both of them to exist first.

9. Run 1 stays ~45 s and banks **one** upgrade (band-1 ore pays 3 P a seam against a 10 P cheapest buy, so this is already close). Late runs 3-5 minutes. The key ratio is shallow-to-deep material value: wrong either way and one of the two axes dies.

Still open, and all of it is tuning rather than design: The heat cost curve (linear per metre past the limit, or accelerating); how a leg escalates east (a curve, or a hand-authored table as `LEVEL_THREATS` does for the campaign's first eleven); and how long a late run really is, which is an output of the costs pass rather than an input to it. [The heat curve has since been settled as the built doubling staircase, so only leg escalation and late-run length remain open.]

06 as shipped (docs/mine-plan.html, half of a pair): the band decides the material, so depth tells you which seam you are looking for, but finding one is a random walk along that band until 08 lands. Expect it to feel unrewarding until then — that is the missing half, not a tuning problem.

STILL OPEN (CLAUDE.md): **A COLONY CAN BOX ITSELF IN.** ... at 45% solid a colony can dig itself into a pocket it cannot leave, which the rock-eating consumables would answer and nothing currently does. Do not "fix" it by relaxing those three [assertions]; they are reporting something.

What is NOT in it yet (CLAUDE.md): **No secrets and no new resource types below** — the owner said they would develop that later, and the bands' `orePerPile` is where the value curve lives when they do.

What is NOT in it yet (CLAUDE.md): **The mine records no high score.** `p.mineBest` is a field of its own — the board is per MODE and ranks survival's level number, so a depth would have to be dressed as a level to get in. (Also: the global leaderboard needs one migration to split by mode.)

What is NOT in it yet (CLAUDE.md): **No `#mine` route in `make-web-zip`'s level prune.** ... the first mine band whose theme the campaign does NOT use will ship as rock you can grow through. Check before the next cut.

Telemetry (CLAUDE.md): What it needs next is TELEMETRY — the whole point of the exercise is "do people play this longer", and `logEvent` currently files a mine run as `game: 'mine'` with no depth on it. The obvious addition is depth reached on `run_end` ... either way `docs/analytics.html` needs a mine column before the first upload can be read.

Balance question left to the owner (CLAUDE.md): **`amputateCharges` MAY NOW BE TOO SMALL: two doses left 28 strands rotten** on a dense map, because narrower passages pack the colony tighter and one breach claims more of it.

mechanisms.name: Fruiting pays for reach: a guaranteed payout on every run, set by how far the colony got
mechanisms.exemplars: Downwell (every gem collected, even spent ones, counts toward unlocks); Rogue Legacy (gold always goes into the manor); Motherload (deeper ore sells for more); idle-game rule of thumb: first upgrade within 60 s
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Every run pays something visible, and run 1 buys its one upgrade because of how the payout is built rather than seam luck. Measured with a bot on the current build: run 1 paid 9 P and 3 P on two saves against a 10 P cheapest rung. One save's first purchase came on run 6; another save had none after 5 runs. The payout also makes depth, the stated goal, the thing that earns. Today deep seams pay zero Phosphorus, so descending earns less of the currency that buys most of the store.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: It is literally 'the colony fruits and spores', and it matches the full-payout ending. It banks in presentMineEnd with the ore, in whole numbers, e.g. +1 P per 5 m, plus P per 100 m east once legs exist. It refuels nothing, so 'nothing worth having on the way down' still holds. Keep it to roughly 30-40% of a typical run's P so lateral seams still matter, and show it as its own line on the end screen.

mechanisms.name: A purchase on every early run: price pass sized to the journey (plan 09)
mechanisms.exemplars: Idle/incremental pacing (first buy under 60 s, a new layer every 3-5 min); Vampire Survivors (an unlock or gold spend after nearly every run); Brotato (a shop between every wave); Dome Keeper (every upgrade must feel meaningfully different)
mechanisms.whyItRetains: A store visit that buys nothing teaches the player the store is not for them. A buy on every one of the first ~10 runs, then one every 2-3, keeps the 'one more run' pull alive through the first hour. CrazyGames benchmarks a 10+ minute average session.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: This is plan item 09. Today about 3,237 P of Phosphorus-priced rungs (the water track alone is 1,849) face roughly 6 P per chunk of band-0 seams (about 126 P in a whole 21-chunk world). Shrink the Phosphorus ladders, or let the reach payout carry supply. Size the whole store to be mostly bought near the promised land. Keep the deep rungs in deep materials and keep run 1 at one upgrade.

mechanisms.name: The journey east: legs, islands, and the promised land as a real ending (plan 07)
mechanisms.exemplars: Slay the Spire acts; Archero chapters; FTL sectors; Hades' escape to the surface; Dome Keeper's relic ending; Loop Hero chapters
mechanisms.whyItRetains: It gives a goal that ENDS, a checkpoint so a failed run still leaves the player further along, and a second axis. Every run then poses one real decision: go down for materials, or right toward the island. That is Dome Keeper's lesson about systems that feed each other. Reaching an island is the win moment the game lacks today: resurface, spore, a big payout, and the next leg revealed on a journey strip.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: This is premise-plan 07 as written: a fresh world per leg seeded by (journey, leg), hill west, island east, the next run starts from the island, no return trips, the 504-column map unchanged. Within the premise: (a) keep each leg's seed fixed across attempts so a retry is mastery, not a reroll; (b) scale the hill-to-island distance by leg index (leg 1 about 5-6 chunks, the full width only on late legs), because the far edge is ~125 lateral digs (~250 water) before maze overhead; (c) answer the open question 'how a leg escalates' with a hand-authored table for legs 1-10, as LEVEL_THREATS did for the campaign.

mechanisms.name: Island compass and per-resource compasses: sell information, not power (plan 08)
mechanisms.exemplars: Terraria Metal Detector (shows the most valuable ore nearby); Spelunky Spectacles/Udjat Eye (reveal treasure in walls); Hollow Knight Cornifer maps and the Wayward Compass; Subnautica scanner room
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Each rung changes how the player plays, not just a number, and turns a random walk into a plan. The bot data shows why this matters: a bot that chased every visible seam did WORSE (6-24 m, 0-3 P) than one that just dove, because reaching things through the maze is where water gets wasted.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: Premise verbatim: bought, nothing given, per resource, rungs direction → +distance → biggest deposit, and it points THROUGH rock as a bearing, never a route. Water is a resource and the fuel, so a water dowser is the natural fifth compass. It completes the 06 pair.

mechanisms.name: Your best, drawn in the world
mechanisms.exemplars: Hill Climb Racing best-distance flag; Trials and Mario Kart time-trial ghosts; high-score lines in endless runners
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Self-competition with a target inside the frame. Near-misses ('4 m short') are the strongest reason to retry, and crossing the line is a free celebration moment.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: p.mineBest is already stored. Draw one labelled line at the deepest depth ever and, on a leg, one at the farthest east, and flash a beat plus a sound when either is crossed. The ground already carries the band beat, so this is the same idea.

mechanisms.name: The previous attempt's colony left as a fossil on the same leg
mechanisms.exemplars: Dark Souls bloodstains and ghosts; Trials ghosts; Rogue Legacy ancestors and graves; Spelunky seeded runs
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Failure becomes map knowledge ('every run counts', the Hades rule). Progress between attempts is visible at a glance, and learning the maze becomes a skill the player can feel growing.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: It is 'the colony IS the map' taken literally, and fixed per-leg seeds make the fossil line up with the world. It is visual only, so there is no return trip and no reuse of tissue. Store a downsampled polyline per (journey, leg) in the save.

mechanisms.name: An end screen that counts up the payout, names the next goal, and buys in one tap
mechanisms.exemplars: Downwell's 'next unlock is close' bar; Balatro's score count-up; the Hades post-death room; Brotato's between-wave shop
mechanisms.whyItRetains: It plants the next goal at the moment motivation peaks ('3 P short of Grow strength', 'island 180 m past your best') and cuts dead time between runs. Today the screen says only '+9' and 'To the store'.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: The end screen stays one sentence plus one button. Add a count-up by source (seams, pockets, reach), the next affordable or nearest rung with an inline Buy, and Descend. The full payout is unchanged.

mechanisms.name: Progressive shelf reveal (unlock cadence)
mechanisms.exemplars: Vampire Survivors' unlock drip; Balatro's growing collection; idle games' revealed layers; Dome Keeper gadgets
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Each reveal is a novelty beat and a reason to come back to the store. It also shrinks the first store to a two-choice decision, against an owner who found the card layer 'too complex'.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: Show Water and Grow strength first. Heat tolerance appears the first time 42 m is crossed, Mucus flasks at the first worm contact, Cutting enzyme at the first mould sighting, and compasses at the first island or deep seam. upgradeInGame is already the single predicate for both the shelf and the buy path. Consumables stay bought.

mechanisms.name: Juice on every payout and every threshold
mechanisms.exemplars: Vampire Survivors chests (slot-machine cadence, from a former slot designer); Balatro scoring; Mr. Driller air capsules worth 100, 200, 300 in sequence
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Moment-to-moment reward is what makes a one-minute run feel full. Today a seam digest or pocket tap only changes a HUD number (mineFrame just sets uiDirty), and the mine's only sound is the grow sample.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: Presentation only. Add sounds for seam, pocket, line crossing, new best, worm attach and an infection tick; +3 P and +10 water floaters using the existing `floaters` system; navigator.vibrate on phones; rising pitch for consecutive seams in one descent.

mechanisms.name: Leg modifiers from a hand-authored table
mechanisms.exemplars: Hades biomes; Slay the Spire acts and bosses; Balatro boss blinds; Brotato danger levels
mechanisms.whyItRetains: It stops ten legs from feeling like one leg ten times. Every new leg is a new 'first', and each one can teach one system: a dry leg teaches pockets, a worm leg teaches flasks, a rot leg teaches the enzyme.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: It answers the plan's open question (a curve or a table like LEVEL_THREATS) with a table. Modifiers use existing knobs only: threatBands, reservoirsPerBand, heat.safeDepth, gallery shape, material richness. Nothing respawns and band 1 stays threat-free on leg 1.

mechanisms.name: Oxalic-acid vial: a bought way through ONE rock, plus an obvious Fruit now
mechanisms.exemplars: Motherload dynamite and C4; Spelunky bombs; SteamWorld Dig's wall-jump, which turned 'stuck' from a binary state into a grey zone
mechanisms.whyItRetains: The box-in dead end becomes a decision instead of dead air. The generator already leaves some seams and pockets walled in as 'visible bait', and this gives the player a reason to buy for them. A Fruit now chip after several refused digs in a row ends a stuck run with a full payout, instead of leaving End run buried in the gear menu.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: The owner said verbatim: 'we will have consumables later that allow people to grow through rocks when needed.' It is scarce, bought, and sold as carry capacity like flasks, so rock stays a wall by default. It is also real biology: fungi weather rock with oxalic acid.

mechanisms.name: Three active missions
mechanisms.exemplars: Jetpack Joyride missions (three at a time); Subway Surfers; Archero daily tasks; Brotato and Vampire Survivors achievement unlocks
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Each run gets its own small story. Missions steer players into systems they would skip (pockets, lateral seams, flasks, curing rot), and they give a near goal while the island is still far off.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: They are goals, not cards, and nothing is drafted. Rewards are Phosphorus or deep materials. Examples: 'tap 2 pockets in one descent', 'reach Anthracite', 'cure an infection before the clock', 'get 300 m east on leg 2'.

mechanisms.name: Secrets in some dead ends, plus a field journal
mechanisms.exemplars: Motherload artifacts (dinosaur bones, treasure); Spelunky secrets and journal; the Hades codex; SteamWorld Dig caves
mechanisms.whyItRetains: A variable reward makes optional spurs worth a gamble. Lore lines about the promised land give the journey a narrative drip at almost no art cost, and the journal is a completion goal once the store is done.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: CLAUDE.md says the owner will develop secrets 'later'. Dead ends currently 'pay nothing' by design, so let a small share hold a rare motherlode seam or a spore relic, still off the descent route.

mechanisms.name: Daily descent on a shared seed
mechanisms.exemplars: Spelunky Daily Challenge; Balatro and Dead Cells seeded runs; the Wordle-style daily ritual
mechanisms.whyItRetains: A reason to come back tomorrow, and a result that can be compared. CrazyGames targets 10-15% day-1 retention and names daily quests and login bonuses as the levers.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: #mine,<seed> is already deterministic. It needs the per-mode leaderboard migration. It is a bonus run, never a gate on normal play.

mechanisms.name: New Journey (ascension) after the promised land
mechanisms.exemplars: Slay the Spire Ascension; Peglin Cruciball; Hades Heat; Brotato Danger 1-5
mechanisms.whyItRetains: A long tail for players who finished, reusing all existing content. It is the answer to store exhaustion.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: Legs are already 'seeded by journey and leg index', so journey N+1 means new seeds plus one added rule each time (drier, hotter lines, earlier worms). Unlock one cosmetic strand tint per journey completed.

mechanisms.name: Island colonies fruit while you are away
mechanisms.exemplars: Archero Hero Patrol; idle games' offline earnings (about 50% rate, capped)
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Reopening the game is rewarded, and being away is never punished.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: 'The colony IS the map, spread across it': every island reached is a colony left behind. Keep it small and capped (e.g. 8 h) so it never replaces playing, and pay in Phosphorus only.

mechanisms.name: Desktop side panels
mechanisms.exemplars: Balatro and Luck be a Landlord side HUDs; portrait games that fill their landscape gutters
mechanisms.whyItRetains: Itch traffic is 81% desktop, and on 1280x720 the portrait column leaves two thirds of the screen black, which reads as unfinished. The panels keep the journey strip, the missions, your best and your compasses always in view.
mechanisms.fitWithPremises: The portrait playfield is untouched; only the empty gutters change.

4.sessionStructure:
A GREAT 5-MINUTE SESSION, first or twentieth: one tap from the portal to the first dig (the title already offers a single DIG door). Then 3-5 descents of 45 s to 2 min each. Every end screen counts the payout up by source (seams, pockets, reach) and names the next goal. Every store visit buys at least one thing. Each session holds at least one 'first': a new band beat, the first worm, a newly revealed track, a leg modifier, or an island reached or visibly closer (the best-line and the fossil of the last attempt show it). The session ends on a near goal ('island 1 is 180 m past your best', '2 Garnet to Grow 5'), so closing the tab feels like pausing, not finishing.

A GREAT FIRST HOUR. 0:00-1:00: run 1 teaches drag-to-dig by doing it, reaches about 45 m, and ends right after the '42 m / Anthracite' beat and the dig price doubling to 4, as a tease. SPORED, the reach payout, one affordable rung highlighted, buy. 1:00-5:00: runs 2-4 buy one thing each; the first worm is met in band 2 and Mucus flasks appear on the shelf. 5:00-12:00: the short leg 1 island is reached: resurface, spore, a big payout, and the journey strip reveals the islands to the promised land; the island compass appears. 12:00-30:00: legs 2-3, each with one named modifier; the first material-priced rung (Anthracite heat tolerance); the first mould breach and its 20 s deadline, cured or taken with a full payout; missions start adding side goals. 30:00-60:00: legs 4-5, the Garnet band visited with a Garnet compass, 20-30 purchases in total, runs now 2-3 minutes, each retry visibly passing the last attempt's fossil.

A GREAT FIRST WEEK. Day 1 return: a daily descent on a shared seed with the best recorded, three fresh missions, and the island colonies' small overnight fruiting to collect; a leg or two per session. Days 2-5: a journey of about 10 legs finishes after roughly 3-5 hours in total. The promised land is a real ending: credits, and every island reached fruiting at once. The store is mostly bought by then, so it never becomes the goal on its own. After: New Journey with one added rule per journey (ascension-style), a cosmetic per journey, field-journal completion and the daily board carry the long tail through mastery rather than grind.
pitfalls: GRIND WALL IN THE CURRENCY. Phosphorus only comes from band-0 seams: 2 per chunk at 3 P, about 6 P per chunk and about 126 P in the whole 21-chunk world. Deep seams pay zero P. Against that, the Phosphorus-priced rungs total about 3,237 P (water track 1,849, ore yield 422, pockets 378, flasks 364). Unfixed, the late game becomes farming the shallowest band, the opposite of 'go deeper' and of 'go down to afford going right'. This is the shallow-to-deep ratio plan 09 warns about; fix it before tuning anything else.

A FIRST STORE VISIT WITH NOTHING TO BUY. A bot on the current build (84 water, 42 digs, 25-37 s at bot pace) banked 9 P and 3 P on run 1 against a 10 P cheapest rung. One save's first purchase came on run 6 of 8; another save bought nothing in 5 runs. Only about 3 band-0 P seams lie within reach of the start. Make run 1's one upgrade a certainty by construction.
STORE EXHAUSTION WITH NOTHING AFTER. Once the tracks cap there is no sink and no goal. The promised-land ending, New Journey, the journal and cosmetics must exist before a player can max the store.

EARLY RUNS ALL LOOK THE SAME. The first 42 m is threat-free on purpose, and 8 bot runs ended at 20-56 m, so the first ten minutes can be the same brown band ten times. Over those runs worms drained 0 to 1.2 water in total and no infection happened, so flasks and the enzyme have no reason to exist yet. Front-load a 'first' into every early run and reveal each track when its threat is met.

OPAQUE REACHABILITY THROUGH THE MAZE. A visible seam can cost the whole tank to reach: a bot that chased seams up to about 950 units away scored worse (6-24 m, 0-3 P) than one that dove. Players read wasted water as unfairness. The compasses (bearing, not route) and a readable 'this is sealed' state are the answer. Do not solve it by selling a route or by opening the maze.

THE BOXED-IN RUN THAT NEVER ENDS. A colony walled in with water left sits refusing digs forever, and End run is buried in the settings gear. Surface a Fruit now chip (full payout) after several refused digs, and plan the owner-sanctioned rock consumable.

SILENT REWARDS. Seam digest and pocket tap only change a HUD number: no sound, no floater, no haptic, even though a floaters system exists. A payout the player does not notice does not work as a reward.

RE-INTRODUCING THE COMPLEXITY THE OWNER REJECTED. No drafting, no deck, no pick-1-of-3 each run ('too complex', 'too much card drafting'). Depth has to come from the map, the two axes (down vs east) and the threats, not from build-crafting. Keep the store's first screen to a couple of choices.

MAKING LOSS HURT. The owner said dying 'felt like you lost too much'. Every ending stays a full payout. Do not add push-your-luck 'lose your haul' mechanics, and never gate play behind energy timers the way Archero does.

REROLLING A FAILED LEG. If a leg's world changes on every attempt, the player cannot learn it and each retry feels like a lottery. Keep leg seeds fixed per (journey, leg) as the premise says, and keep the per-seed depth-per-dig spread small (CLAUDE.md measured 1.4x after aiming).

A FIRST ISLAND THAT ARRIVES AN HOUR IN. Reaching the far east edge of a 504-column world takes about 125 lateral digs (about 250 water) before maze overhead. If leg 1 is that long, the game's first real win lands long after most portal players have left (CrazyGames benchmarks a 10+ min average session). Scale the hill-to-island distance by leg index, and put the first island inside the first 5-12 minutes.

RUN LENGTH DRIFTING OFF ITS PREMISE. startWater has moved 20 → 30 → 44 → 84 as the carve changed, so run 1 is now 42 digs: roughly 55-90 s at a human drag pace against 'under a minute / ~45 s'. Re-measure with a human-paced drag, not the probe. Lock the leg geometry before pricing the economy, because every carve change has moved the tank.

DESKTOP DEAD SPACE. At 1280x720 the portrait column uses about a third of the screen and the rest is black. Itch traffic is 81% desktop. Use the gutters for the journey strip, missions and best instead of leaving them empty.

SHIPPING BLIND. run_end still carries no depth, leg or purchase data, so 'do people play this longer' cannot be answered after the upload. Ship depth/leg/purchase telemetry with the journey. Never average itch and CrazyGames: they behave like different games.
MINOR: on a 390 px phone the grown 'SPORED' wordmark touches or clips both screen edges on the end screen.
